title: Circuit simulation of an oblivious computation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite binary Turing machine whose input-head position and work-tape head positions after any fixed number of steps depend only on the input length. Suppose $M$ decides a language $L$ within time $T$. Then there is a constant $K\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $n$, there is a well-formed Boolean circuit with at most two inputs per gate, size at most $K(T(n)+n+1)$, and output on each $n$-bit input $x$ equal to the indicator of whether $x\in L$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite binary Turing machine
$M$ is oblivious: equal-length inputs have identical input-head and work-head positions at every step
$L$ is a language over the binary alphabet
